title: Hip joint and blood supply of the femoral head (intracapsular fracture)

related.id: MB-231 Hip fracture in an older patient
related.why: Perioperative management of a displaced intracapsular fracture
Another bone whose blood supply fails after fracture

brief.scenario: Mrs Irene Ormerod, 81, fell at home and has a displaced intracapsular fracture of her left femoral neck. Before the fall she lived alone and walked to the shops with a stick.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the hip joint and the blood supply of the femoral head, and relate them to her fracture.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: The head's blood runs up the neck inside the capsule: break the neck, displace it, and the head starves.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Relying on the artery of the ligamentum teres to keep an adult femoral head alive.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll start with the joint and its capsule, then its blood supply, then relate both to her fracture."

grid.label: Joint type and surfaces
grid.fail: Calls it a hinge joint, or can't name the articulating surfaces.
grid.pass: Synovial ball-and-socket joint between the femoral head and acetabulum, deepened by the fibrocartilaginous labrum.
grid.high: Explains its stability: deep socket, labrum and strong capsular ligaments, at the cost of less range than the shoulder.

grid.label: Capsule and ligaments
grid.pass: Iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments thicken the capsule; ligamentum teres runs to the fovea.
grid.high: Iliofemoral (Y-shaped, AIIS to intertrochanteric line) is very strong and limits hyperextension; most of the neck lies inside the capsule.

grid.label: Blood supply of the femoral head
grid.fail: Names only the obturator artery or the profunda.
grid.pass: Mainly the medial circumflex femoral artery, via retinacular (ascending cervical) branches running up the neck.
grid.high: Deep branch of the MFCA pierces the capsule and runs up the posterosuperior neck as retinacular vessels; ligamentum teres artery adds little in adults.

grid.label: Why the head dies
grid.fail: Thinks the artery of the ligamentum teres will keep the head alive.
grid.pass: Displacement tears the retinacular vessels, so the head risks avascular necrosis and the fracture non-union.
grid.high: Contrasts extracapsular fractures, which spare these vessels, so fixation works there but not in displaced intracapsular fractures.

grid.label: Classifying the fracture
grid.borderline: Recites Garden I–IV but can't group them into undisplaced and displaced, which is what decides treatment.
grid.pass: Intracapsular; Garden I–II undisplaced, III–IV displaced. Hers is displaced.
grid.high: Defines each: I incomplete valgus-impacted, II complete undisplaced, III partly displaced, IV fully displaced.

grid.label: Surgical choice for a displaced fracture
grid.fail: Plans screw fixation for a displaced intracapsular fracture in an 81-year-old.
grid.pass: Replacement arthroplasty (hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement), cemented, on the day of or after admission.
grid.high: Considers total hip replacement: she walked outdoors with a stick, and if fit and expected to stay independent beyond 2 years.

grid.label: Undisplaced intracapsular fracture
grid.fail: Replaces every intracapsular fracture regardless of displacement.
grid.pass: Undisplaced fractures keep more of their supply and are usually fixed: multiple cancellous (cannulated) screws or a sliding hip screw.
grid.high: Knows NICE lists the best treatment of undisplaced intracapsular fractures as a research question.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What type of joint is the hip?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A synovial ball-and-socket joint: femoral head in the acetabulum, deepened by the fibrocartilaginous labrum. The deep socket, labrum and capsule make it stable, with less range than the shoulder.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Iliofemoral, pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments in the capsule. The iliofemoral is Y-shaped, from the anterior inferior iliac spine to the intertrochanteric line; it is very strong and limits hyperextension. Most of the neck is inside the capsule. The ligamentum teres runs to the fovea.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The medial circumflex femoral artery, mainly: its deep branch pierces the capsule and divides into retinacular vessels that climb the posterosuperior neck to the head. In adults, the artery of the ligamentum teres adds little.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Why does that matter for her?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Displacement tears the retinacular vessels, so the head is at risk of avascular necrosis and non-union. Extracapsular fractures spare them, which is why those are fixed and displaced intracapsular ones aren't.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Her X-ray shows a displaced subcapital fracture. Classify it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Intracapsular. Garden I is incomplete and valgus-impacted, II complete but undisplaced, III partly displaced, IV fully displaced. Hers is displaced, III or IV.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Cemented arthroplasty on the day of or the day after admission. She walked outdoors with no more than a stick, so if she has no condition that makes it unsuitable and should stay independent beyond 2 years, I'd consider total hip replacement rather than hemiarthroplasty.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Usually fixed, with cannulated screws or a sliding hip screw. NICE lists the best treatment for undisplaced fractures as a research question.

failures.move: Saying the artery of the ligamentum teres will keep the head alive after a displaced fracture.
failures.consequence: The candidate can't explain why these fractures are replaced, not fixed.

failures.move: Fixing a displaced intracapsular fracture with screws in an older patient.
failures.consequence: High risk of avascular necrosis, non-union and a second operation; NICE says offer arthroplasty.

failures.move: Not distinguishing intracapsular from extracapsular fractures.
failures.consequence: Leads to the wrong operation, because the blood supply is what differs.

recovery.when: You lose track of the arteries
recovery.line: The key point: most of the head's blood comes from the medial circumflex, climbing the neck inside the capsule.

recovery.when: You can't recall the Garden grades
recovery.line: What drives treatment is whether it's displaced: displaced intracapsular fractures are replaced.

knowledge.fact: The deep branch of the medial circumflex femoral artery is the main supply to the femoral head: inside the capsule it runs up the posterosuperior neck as two to four retinacular vessels.
In adults the artery of the ligamentum teres (from the obturator) supplies only a small area of the head near the fovea.
Displaced intracapsular fractures disrupt the retinacular vessels: avascular necrosis and non-union after fixation.

Displaced intracapsular: offer arthroplasty; consider THR if walking outdoors with no more than a stick, no unsuitable comorbidity, and independent beyond 2 years. Cemented implants. Surgery on the day of or after admission.

recall.think: Avascular necrosis and non-union if a displaced intracapsular fracture is fixed.
recall.say: "Displaced intracapsular: the retinacular vessels are torn, so she needs a cemented arthroplasty."

numbers.meaning: surgery on the day of or after admission

recall.trap: The ligamentum teres artery won't save an adult femoral head.
recall.finish: Cemented hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement.

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination
sources.supports: Station format: 9 minutes with 1 minute's reading; examiner-led questioning in applied knowledge stations

sources.name: Gray's Anatomy for Students (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)
sources.supports: Hip joint: synovial ball-and-socket joint between the head of the femur and the acetabulum, deepened by the fibrocartilaginous acetabular labrum; stability from the deep socket, labrum and strong capsular ligaments; capsule attached to the intertrochanteric line anteriorly and to the neck posteriorly, so most of the neck is intracapsular; iliofemoral (Y-shaped, from the ilium below the anterior inferior iliac spine to the intertrochanteric line), pubofemoral and ischiofemoral ligaments reinforce the capsule and tighten in extension; ligament of the head of the femur runs from the acetabular notch to the fovea and carries the artery to the head from the obturator artery; the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries supply the joint, with retinacular vessels running along the neck inside the capsule

sources.name: NICE CG124: Hip fracture: management
sources.supports: Surgery on the day of, or the day after, admission (1.2.1); operate to allow full weight bearing immediately after surgery (1.6.1); offer replacement arthroplasty (total hip replacement or hemiarthroplasty) for displaced intracapsular fracture (1.6.2); consider total hip replacement rather than hemiarthroplasty if the person was able to walk independently out of doors with no more than a stick, has no condition or comorbidity making it unsuitable, and is expected to carry out activities of daily living independently beyond 2 years (1.6.3, 2023); cemented implants (1.6.4); management of undisplaced intracapsular fractures is a research recommendation

sources.name: Gautier E, Ganz K, Krügel N, Gill T, Ganz R. Anatomy of the medial femoral circumflex artery and its surgical implications. J Bone Joint Surg Br 2000;82(5):679-83 (PMID 10963165)
sources.supports: The primary source of blood supply to the femoral head is the deep branch of the medial femoral circumflex artery; it perforates the joint capsule at the level of gemellus superior and, in its intracapsular segment, runs along the posterosuperior aspect of the femoral neck, dividing into two to four subsynovial retinacular vessels

sources.name: Trueta J, Harrison MHM. The normal vascular anatomy of the femoral head in adult man. J Bone Joint Surg Br 1953;35-B(3):442-61 (PMID 13084696)
sources.supports: In the adult femoral head, the lateral epiphyseal (superior retinacular) vessels supply most of the head; the medial epiphyseal vessels entering through the ligamentum teres supply only a limited area adjacent to the fovea

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Displaced intracapsular fractures disrupt the retinacular blood supply to the femoral head, risking avascular necrosis and non-union after fixation; extracapsular fractures leave this supply intact and are fixed

sources.name: Garden RS. Low-angle fixation in fractures of the femoral neck. J Bone Joint Surg Br 1961;43-B(4):647-63
sources.supports: Garden stages of femoral neck fracture: I incomplete (abduction or valgus-impacted); II complete without displacement; III complete with partial displacement; IV complete with full displacement

sources.name: Frandsen PA, Andersen E, Madsen F, Skjødt T. Garden's classification of femoral neck fractures: an assessment of inter-observer variation. J Bone Joint Surg Br 1988;70(4):588-90 (PMID 3403602)
sources.supports: Groups Garden stages 1 and 2 as undisplaced and stages 3 and 4 as displaced fractures; observers agreed poorly on the individual stages, and 45 of 100 fractures were called undisplaced by some observers and displaced by others

sources.name: Fixation using Alternative Implants for the Treatment of Hip fractures (FAITH) Investigators. Fracture fixation in the operative management of hip fractures (FAITH): an international, multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet 2017;389(10078):1519-27 (PMID 28262269)
sources.supports: Low-energy femoral neck fractures in patients aged 50 or over requiring fixation: multiple small-diameter cancellous screws are the standard of care, compared with a sliding hip screw; no difference in reoperation at 24 months; avascular necrosis more common with the sliding hip screw (9% vs 5%)

partner.opening: Mrs Ormerod has a displaced intracapsular fracture. What type of joint is the hip?

reveals.finding: Ask, without naming them: which ligament reinforces the front of the capsule, running from the anterior inferior iliac spine to the intertrochanteric line? Then: which artery winds behind the femoral neck and sends branches up the neck, inside the capsule, to the head?

Read out: AP pelvis X-ray. On the left, a fracture line crosses the femoral neck immediately below the head. There is no bony contact across the fracture: the shaft and distal neck are shifted upwards and rotated outwards, and the trabecular lines of the head no longer line up with those of the neck. The trochanters are intact.

reveals.trigger: Asks about her function and health
reveals.finding: Walked to the shops with a stick; lived alone, independent with washing and dressing. Treated hypertension. Alert and orientated.

push.question: Why won't the ligamentum teres save her femoral head?
push.expect: Its artery contributes little in adults; the head relies on retinacular branches of the medial circumflex, torn by displacement.

push.question: Hemiarthroplasty or total hip replacement?
push.expect: Consider THR: walks outdoors with no more than a stick, no unsuitable comorbidity, expected to be independent beyond 2 years; cemented.

push.question: How would you treat an undisplaced intracapsular fracture?
push.expect: Usually internal fixation with cannulated screws or a sliding hip screw; NICE has made this a research question.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Extracapsular: the retinacular supply is intact, so the fracture is fixed rather than replaced.

curveballs.prompt: She has mild dementia. Does that rule out a total hip replacement?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not by itself: NICE's 2023 criteria are outdoor walking with no more than a stick, no unsuitable comorbidity, and expected independence beyond 2 years.
